ruling.recommended_action: Close the case with no refund — the sole off-route segment was covered by the rider's own pre-segment general route choice, and no other clause waives the fare.
ruling.reasoning:
One off-route segment exists: 15:21–15:30, 6.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.71 km, +3.60 km, reaching 1425 m from the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 a segment is unexempted only if none of RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it, and only then do its extra km become refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][RD-1].

RD-4 gives no exemption: the only accepted ground is a DataMall incident on the replaced optimal stretch reported before the detour, and none was logged during the trip window [F15][RD-4]. The Pan Island Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 14:46–15:21 is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and does not exempt the segment by itself [F12][RD-4]. The driver's stated reason is therefore not made out on paper, but that does not by itself settle the segment.

RD-3 is not engaged: the rider named no place and no stop is measured in the segment; her message is a route choice, not a stop request [F3][F9][RD-3].

On RD-5 the rider did send the message before the segment started: at 15:18, answering the driver's 15:17 question about PIE traffic, she wrote “Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.” [F8][F9][F10]. That is a general route choice — “whichever way is faster” — i.e. authorisation to choose the route to reach the destination, not a stop away from the route and not a loop of the driver's own [F8][F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record places the driven path somewhere else, and by contrast with a specific-road consent there is no named road to be tied or untied here, so the general authorisation is read on its words as covering the route the driver chose to get to Kallang Wave Mall. The segment therefore stands exempt under RD-5, no unexempted segment remains, and the RD-2 mileage refund is $0 [F3][F9][RD-2]. The rider's point that the segment was longer and the trip ran 46.8 min against a 32.7 min estimate [F2] does not change the scope reading of the words she used; it is reflected in the driver-record note above, not in the fare.

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider “said any faster way was fine, so I went round” is a claim, not consent — consent must be the rider's own message before the segment, and only F9 qualifies; the finding does not rest on F11 [F10][F11][RD-5].

The metered waiting unit $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) stands on a RydeTAXI fare; the rider did not claim it back [F5][RD-3]. Other RydeTAXI meter components (base, distance, time) follow the meter structure and are not re-priced under RD-2 beyond the unexempted-segment formula, and the frozen base fare leaves the segment finding without effect on the amount [F7][RD-2][NS-7].

No account flag: the driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes but 0 upheld (route 0) [F18], so the RD-6 repeated-breach condition is not met and profile facts do not decide the case [F17][F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message at 15:18, “Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.” [F9], answers the driver's 15:17 question about PIE traffic [F8] and was sent before the segment start of 15:21 [F3][F10]. It is a general route choice — authorisation to pick the way to the destination — not a driver's own stop or a loop that reaches nothing, so under RD-5 the route-change segment is not a deviation and its extra km are exempt [F3][F9][RD-5]. No incident exemption is available [F15][RD-4], and the driver's post-trip statement is not the source of this finding [F11][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The existence of the segment [F3] is accepted, but it is exempt, not unexempted: the rider's own 15:18 message [F9], sent before the 15:21 segment start [F3][F10], is a general route choice covering the route the driver took to the destination, so the RD-1 unexempted-deviation step fails [F9][RD-1][RD-5].

The RD-2 mileage formula applies only to an unexempted segment; here the segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][F9][RD-5], so no part of the billed distance excess of $5.88 for 4.17 km is refundable [F4][RD-2].

The rider's message is correctly read as a general authorisation rather than a named road [F9], but that reading makes the segment exempt rather than payable: a general route choice is not limited to a named road and nothing in the record places the driven path outside it [F3][F9][RD-5].

The rider's premise that the authorisation fails because the trip was slower (46.8 min vs 32.7 min estimate) [F2] does not limit the words she used; “whichever way is faster” is an authorisation of route choice, and scope is read from the words, not from the outcome [F9][F2][RD-5].

The computation $3.60 km × $1.4100/km = $5.08 [F3][F4][F7] would be correct only if the segment counted; it is exempt under RD-5 [F9][F3][RD-5], so the refund is $0, and the metered waiting unit $0.11 stands in any event [F5][RD-3].

The claimed RD-4 exemption is not made out: no DataMall incident was logged on the replaced optimal stretch during the trip window [F15], and PIE band 2 [F12] is corroboration only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt a segment alone [F15][F12][RD-4]. The ruling does not rest on RD-4.

The driver's alternative framing that the rest of the +4.1 km is corridor noise [F1][F4] is not needed: the single recorded segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][F9][RD-5], and the remaining gap over the optimal route is within the 200 m matching corridor and not refunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].
